findings.heading: Overview / Обзор
findings.proposition: The English states indirect standardization is preferable when the counts WITHIN each stratum are small ('small numbers per stratum'); the Russian states it is preferable when the NUMBER OF STRATA is small ('в случае небольшого числа страт').
findings.reader_consequence: A Russian reader learns the wrong selection rule for indirect standardization. They will use direct standardization on sparse strata (exactly the case the English warns produces unstable estimates from sampling variation), and may wrongly switch to indirect standardization merely because their stratification is coarse.

findings.heading: Load population data / Загружаем популяционные данные
findings.proposition: The Russian says the chunk that follows consists of `import()` commands ('выполнив следующие команды `import()`'), but the chunk beside it (ru lines 57-73) contains only `appliedepidata::get_data()` calls; the English correctly names `appliedepidata::get_data()`.
findings.reader_consequence: A Russian reader looking for the named function in the code below finds no `import()` call, and may go looking for a rio::import() route that this page no longer uses, instead of learning the `appliedepidata::get_data(name = ...)` pattern the whole handbook now relies on.

findings.heading: Load population data / Загружаем популяционные данные
findings.proposition: The Russian adds that the data are loaded 'from our Github repository' ('из нашего репозитория Github'); the English says only that the data can be loaded directly into R and names no source repository.
findings.reader_consequence: A Russian reader believes the example data are fetched over the network from a GitHub repository. The `appliedepidata::get_data()` call reads from an installed R package, so a reader without network access, or one who tries to browse to the repository to find the files, is misdirected.

findings.heading: Load population data / Загружаем популяционные данные
findings.proposition: The Russian comment above the `world_standard_population_by_sex` load reads 'импорт демографических данных по стране B' (import of demographic data for country B); the English comment on the same line reads 'reference (world standard) population', and the code loads the reference population, not country B demographics.
findings.reader_consequence: A Russian reader sees two consecutive chunk lines both labelled 'demographic data for country B' (ru lines 64 and 70) and no label for the reference population at all. They can mistake `standard_pop_data` for a second country-B demographic object, which breaks their understanding of every later step that joins the standard population.

findings.heading: Load population data / Загружаем популяционные данные
findings.proposition: The English links the phrase 'Download handbook and data' to the page `data_used.qmd`; the Russian carries the label with no link target ('[Скачивание руководства и данных]'), so the cross-reference is absent.
findings.reader_consequence: The Russian page renders the literal text '[Скачивание руководства и данных]' with no hyperlink, so a reader who needs the download instructions has no route to that page and must search the handbook by hand.

findings.heading: Clean populations and deaths / Вычищаем данные по населению и смертям
findings.proposition: The English links 'Pivoting data' to the page `pivoting.qmd` for more detail on the pivot step; the Russian carries the label with no link target ('[Поворот данных]').
findings.reader_consequence: A Russian reader who does not understand `pivot_longer()` is told a fuller explanation exists but is given no way to reach it; the text renders as literal brackets rather than a link.

findings.heading: Clean populations and deaths / Вычищаем данные по населению и смертям
findings.proposition: The English links 'Factors' to the page `factors.qmd` where `fct_relevel()` is described; the Russian carries the label with no link target ('[Факторы]').
findings.reader_consequence: A Russian reader cannot reach the Factors page from the point where factor level ordering is introduced, and loses the explanation of `fct_relevel()` that the English promises there.

findings.heading: Clean reference population / Вычистка референтной популяции
findings.proposition: The English links 'Characters and strings' to the page `characters_strings.qmd` where `str_replace_all()` is described; the Russian carries the label with no link target ('[Текст и последовательности]').
findings.reader_consequence: A Russian reader cannot reach the string-handling page from the `str_replace_all()` step, which is also the page needed to understand the escaping caution two paragraphs later (ru line 279).
